lessons.symptom: A temporary blueprint transformer cannot initialize and reports multiple scenario validation problems before its generator code executes.
lessons.rootCause: The generator's JavaScript source contained literal future mappings such as {{10.body}}, {{11.result.properties}} and {{12.result}}. Make parsed those tokens as mappings of the CURRENT generator scenario, where modules 10/11/12 do not exist.
lessons.failedApproach: Embed literal {{futureModule.field}} tokens directly inside code that is itself stored in a Make mapper.
lessons.fix: Construct future mapping tokens only at runtime, e.g. by concatenating brace characters and module/path strings. Keep current-scenario mappings literal only when the referenced module actually exists in the generator.
lessons.evidence: TMP BG89 blueprint reader 7164847 previously failed run 7864154d78cc4a94a5805b6b4e8e5851 with four blueprint validation problems. After replacing literal future mapping tokens with runtime string construction, execution addaff55c3fd4d0498f727e096bab80c succeeded and returned PARITY_BLUEPRINT_READY with scorer code lengths 10145 and 3254.
lessons.prevention: Generated Make blueprints must separate generator-time mappings from generated-scenario mappings; regression-test the generator itself before creating the target scenario.

lessons.symptom: A field-projected Notion query returns 400 malformed schema because a scorer dependency refers to a property no longer present in the current data-source schema.
lessons.rootCause: Production scoring code can contain legacy/fallback property names even when the live Notion schema has evolved. Blindly converting every get('field') dependency into filter_properties[] treats code dependencies as proof of current schema existence.
lessons.failedApproach: Build projection directly from scorer source references without validating each property against the current Notion data-source schema.
lessons.fix: Compute projection = scorer dependencies intersect current schema properties, then add only current identity/idempotency fields. Missing legacy dependencies remain null/fallback at runtime exactly as production already experiences them.
lessons.evidence: BG89 62/64 scorer dependency extraction plus live Datahub schema read found 437 properties and exactly one missing legacy dependency: Action Score. Including it caused execution 8a74d36936f6461c8c33698f9d914cec to fail 400. Removing only that proven missing property produced execution 86c800afaa6d46328cdf471734cb8ea2: 5 bounded eligible records, 2 ops, 3 credits, 45635 bytes, no writes.
lessons.prevention: Every generated Notion field projection performs dependency ∩ current-schema validation before canary or production promotion.

lessons.symptom: A cost shadow migration risks silently changing business scoring when long deterministic formulas are manually copied or reconstructed from truncated connector output.
lessons.rootCause: Large scorer modules are too error-prone to retype and connector summaries may truncate their source.
lessons.failedApproach: Manually reconstruct the 10k+ character scoring formula from snippets or memory.
lessons.fix: Read the exact current production blueprint through Make /v2/scenarios/{id}/blueprint, copy the scorer modules byte-for-byte into an isolated no-write parity scenario, and change only their input source/mappings required for shadow testing.
lessons.evidence: Production BG89 module 2 code length 10145 and module 5 code length 3254 were extracted from the official blueprint. Transformer execution addaff55c3fd4d0498f727e096bab80c generated an exact no-write parity blueprint, and Make created inactive on-demand scenario 7164938 from it.
lessons.prevention: For long business-rule modules, source parity is blueprint-derived and code-length/hash checked; no manual rewrite is accepted as parity evidence.

protected_rule: Shadow scenarios stay no-write and inactive/on-demand until exact output parity is proven on representative real records. Production ownership does not move on read/query success alone.
